The user wants a very specific output format: labeled sections starting with VERDICT:, no chain-of-thought preamble. Sections: VERDICT, REASONING, NEXT_STEPS, CALL_BACK_IF, RISKS.

Context: Kalshi daily HIGH/LOW weather markets, ~19 US cities, multi-model NWP ensemble. They have model_skill Stage1 leaderboard with walk-forward bias-corrected Brier/CRPS, residual_std.json per (city, mtype, model, lead_bucket), EMOS on ensemble mean, kind-vote blending, Stage3 skill-weighted blend not built, daily calibration broken (overconfident... wait "NO overconfident" — probably means market is not overconfident? Actually "Daily cal broken (NO overconfident)" likely means reliability diagram shows forecasts overconfident — the "(NO overconfident)" is cryptic. Possibly "NOAA overconfident"? Or calibration shows model overconfident. I'll interpret: daily probability calibration is broken — forecasts are overconfident relative to outcomes. Hourly calibrated but no edge after fees. Autopilot + gates; 0 ARMED cells — good, nothing armed.

They ask 4 questions:
1) Best way to choose models/kind groups per city — equal blend, kind-vote, skill-weighted, city-specific subsets?
2) How to discover best combo per city rigorously (data, metrics, leakage rules)?
3) Is residual_std used correctly given EMOS spread c? Learn/adapt/inflate/simplify?
4) Ordered implementation plan that doesn't arm trades until proven.

They want concrete, ordered, reuse walk-forward machinery.

I should answer concisely but substantively. Output only labeled sections. VERDICT first — short overall answer: skill-weighted blend with per-(city,mtype) selection via walk-forward, top-k greedy forward selection with CRPS/Brier objective, keep EMOS but reconcile residual_std with EMOS variance (avoid double counting), gated promotion.

REASONING: answer the four questions with justification.

NEXT_STEPS: ordered implementation plan.

CALL_BACK_IF: conditions to revisit/escalate (e.g., Brier degradation, calibration slope off, sample size insufficient, drift).

RISKS: overfitting per-city subsets, leakage, double-counted spread, small samples, fee drag, market selection bias, regime change.

Let me think through the technical content carefully.

Q1: Choosing models per city.

Recommendation: Two-stage: (a) per (city, mtype, lead_bucket) skill-weighted blending over individual models using walk-forward weights (e.g., weights ∝ exp(-CRPS/T) or inverse-Brier, or nonnegative least squares / constrained ridge on CRPS), with shrinkage toward equal-weight or kind-group prior; (b) model inclusion via greedy forward selection with a complexity penalty. City-specific subsets only where sample sizes support it (per city per mtype maybe ~100-300 daily obs/year; HIGH/LOW two mtypes; 19 cities — enough if pooling across seasons with care). Prefer pooling: hierarchical/partial pooling — city-specific weights shrunk toward global (or climate-region) weights. Kind-vote as a regularizer/prior, not final: use kind-group means as base learners alongside top individual models.

Ensemble combination literature: equal-weight often beats estimated weights at small n ("forecast combination puzzle"). So: start with skill-trimmed equal-weight (drop models that are dominated), then move to shrunk skill weights. Weight estimator: minimize walk-forward CRPS subject to simplex constraints (stacked regressions / "stacking" / nonlinear CRPS minimization), or exponential weights (exponentially weighted average forecaster, learning rate tuned). Given existing model_skill machinery with walk-forward Brier/CRPS per model, easiest: weights w_i ∝ max(0, skill_i - skill_baseline)^p normalized, computed out-of-sample, refit monthly/quarterly.

Also per lead_bucket since relative skill changes with lead. Use (city, mtype, lead_bucket) but pool across lead within bucket.

Q2: Rigorous combo discovery.

Data: archived forecasts per model per issuance time aligned to actual valid date and settlement (official obs/climo station used by Kalshi settlement — must match settlement source exactly). Use recorder-native actuals. Minimum ~2 years to include seasonal variation; define folds.

Metrics: primary = Brier score on the traded event bins (market-relevant thresholds) and CRPS of predictive distribution; plus calibration (reliability slope, PIT histogram), log score for tails; economic: simulated edge after fees with gate rules. Use Diebold-Mariano test for comparing combos; block bootstrap by date for CIs.

Leakage rules: strictly walk-forward — weights at time t estimated only on data < t; freeze hyperparameters (top-k, shrinkage λ, learning rate) chosen on an inner validation window (nested walk-forward), not on the final test; no using same-day other-city info improperly (fine actually, same-day cross-city is available at forecast time — allowed as features but not in fitting unless timestamped); bias-correction coefficients fit within training window only; EMOS coefficients fit trailing window; settlement source alignment; avoid survivorship (models entering/exiting archive); dedupe correlated models (ARPEGE/ECMWF correlated)
